pages.text: The $(thing)Bloomery$() is a device used to smelt $(thing)Iron Ore$() into $(thing)Iron Blooms$() which can be worked into $(thing)Wrought Iron$(). Some common iron ores are $(item)Hematite$(), $(item)Limonite$(), and $(item)Magnetite$(). These ores melt into $(thing)Cast Iron$() rather than $(thing)Wrought Iron$(). All iron-bearing items melt into Cast Iron. To turn them into usable iron, the bloomery is needed. Any iron item can be used in the bloomery, including iron tools and cast iron ingots!

The bloomery is made from 8 $(thing)Bronze Double Plates$(). Which is a total of 32 bronze ingots.$(br)The bloomery will also need $(t:#tfc:bloomery_insulation)22 stone blocks$() such as stone bricks.

pages.name: Bloomery Structure
pages.text: A full size bloomery. The bloomery block will open and close with $(item)$(k:key.use)$().

The bloomery can contain up to a maximum of 48 $(thing)Inputs$(), with 16 items per layer of the chimney; 8 charcoal and 8 iron containing items.$(br2)To add items to the bloomery, climb up to the top and throw items inside with $(item)$(k:key.drop)$(). A tower of grey ore should form.$(br2)You can only use $(item)Charcoal$() as fuel for your bloomery.
The bloomery consumes $(thing)1 Charcoal$() and $(thing)144 mB of Cast Iron$() to produce one $(thing)Bloom$().

Most iron dust contains 129mB of iron, so unless you are using pure cast iron ingots, we recommend $(item)25 metal ore dusts$() and $(item)22 charcoal$() for a full bloomery. This will incur a loss of 57mB of iron.$(br)After filling the bloomery with a combination of $(thing)Fuel$() and $(thing)Ore$(), light the bloomery doors, and wait $(t:12.5 min)$(6)15 in-game hours$() for the bloomery to smelt. When the bloomery shuts off, it leaves behind a $(thing)Bloom$() block. This contains hot $(thing)Raw Iron Blooms$() which can be obtained by mining the $(thing)Bloom$() repeatedly with a pickaxe.
Remember that a little iron waste is not worth your time worrying about!
pages.title: Bloomery Ratios

pages.text: The $(thing)Raw Iron Bloom$() must be worked in a $(l:craftsmanship/anvils)Anvil$() to make $(thing)Refined Iron Bloom$(). And then that must be worked again into $(thing)Wrought Iron Ingots$().$(br)It is recommended to use $(l:craftsmanship/anvils#helve_hammer)Helve Hammers$() to automate the refining steps.

$(li)If the bloomery finds contains more items than it can handle it will try to spit them out the front.$(li)To retrieve your items from a bloomery that is not lit; break the bloomery block.$(li)Blooms will only melt into cast iron, not wrought iron. They must be worked!$(li)Snow accumulation can ruin a bloomerys process.
pages.title: Bloomery Tips
Steam Bloomery
pages.text: Available with the creation of $(item)Black Steel$()―is the Steam Bloomery. This structure―added by $(bold)$(#ff0fb7)TerraFirma$(#595959)Greg$()―is capable of producing blooms automatically, on top of being faster and more efficently than the traditional bloomery by using high-pressure steam.

pages.name: Structure
pages.text: A steam bloomery requires item input and item output buses, and a steam input hatch.
